newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan May export orders up 4.21 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan May export orders up 4.21 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 4.21 percent to US$10.45 billion in May compared to May 1996, the economics ministry said on Saturday, reaffirming a figure disclosed informally on Friday.
The closely watched indicator came in somewhat below an average 5.082 percent year-on-year forecast compiled from a June 19 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
In month-to-month terms, the May upturn lagged April's 5.91 percent annual rise.
At US$10.45 billion, the total marked the third consecutive month in which Taiwan's export orders had exceeded US$10 billion, the ministry said.
The following is a table of export order data in million of U.S. dollars:

Geographically, the Untied States remained Taiwan's biggest market with export orders rising 11.62 percent to US$3.228 billion. Informational and telecommunication products topped the island's main exports to the United States.
Hong Kong was next with orders totalling US$1.885 billion, up 4.96 percent from May 1996.

Orders from Japan, Taiwan's main pork export destination, were down 18.71 percent to US$1.225 billion due to an official ban on Taiwan pork imports following Taiwan's March outbreak of a hog foot and mouth disease.
European orders rose a scant 0.13 percent to US$1.491 billion.
In sectoral term, telecommunication and information products orders rose 8.54 percent to US$1.653 billion, followed by electronics products, up 9.59 percent to US$1.474 billion.
Textile orders grew 17.68 percent to US$1.431 billion, while base metal products increased 23.43 percent to US$922 million.
Plastics and rubber orders rose 6.81 percent to US$690 million, while machinery orders were down 12.16 percent to US$686 million.
